name: Question 18
problem:
Let $V=C[0,1]$ be the vector space of all functions that are continuous on $[0,1],$ equipped with the inner product 

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩={\int }_{0}^{1}x(t)y(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Normalize the vector $f(t)=1-\sqrt{t}.$
worked_solution:
The norm of a vector $f(t)$ with respect to an inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ is defined as

$$
‖f(t)‖=\sqrt{⟨f(t),f(t)⟩}.
$$

Computing the inner product using our definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨f(t),f(t)⟩ & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{(1-\sqrt{t})}^{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\,(1-2\sqrt{t}+t),\text{d}t \\  & ={(t-\frac{4{t}^{3/2}}{3}+\frac{{t}^{2}}{2})|}_{0}^{1}\,\text{d}t \\  & =1-\frac{4}{3}+\frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
‖f(t)‖=\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}.
$$

To normalize the vector $f(t),$ we divide $f(t)$ by its norm $‖f(t)‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}u(t) & =\frac{f(t)}{‖f(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{(1-\sqrt{t})}{\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}} \\  & =\sqrt{6}(1-\sqrt{t})\end{aligned}
$$

⟨x(t),y(t)⟩=∫01x(t)y(t)dt.

Normalize the vector f(t)=1−t.

EXPLANATION

The norm of a vector f(t) with respect to an inner product ⟨⋅,⋅⟩ is defined as

‖f(t)‖=⟨f(t),f(t)⟩.

Computing the inner product using our definition, we get

⟨f(t),f(t)⟩=∫01(1−t)2dt=∫01(1−2t+t),dt=(t−4t3/23+t22)|01dt=1−43+12=16.

Therefore,

‖f(t)‖=16.

To normalize the vector f(t), we divide f(t) by its norm ‖f(t)‖:

u(t)=f(t)‖f(t)‖=(1−t)16=6(1−t)
